question: Should OpenClaw officially bundle and own an agent-facing broker that intentionally exposes approved raw 1Password values to model turns?
rationale: The plugin boundary is technically appropriate, but VISION.md sets a high bar for bundling optional plugins and this capability becomes part of the credential trust boundary; implementation review cannot decide that ownership commitment.

options.title: Sponsor the bundled broker
options.body: Accept OpenClaw ownership after fixing activation behavior, obtaining live security proof, and assigning ongoing approval and credential-boundary ownership.

options.title: Publish through ClawHub
options.body: Keep the same plugin architecture in an owner-maintained external repository and use ClawHub for provenance, review, and distribution.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bundled broker
recommendation.body: Accept OpenClaw ownership after fixing activation behavior, obtaining live security proof, and assigning ongoing approval and credential-boundary ownership.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest combined history across current secrets documentation, plugin-manifest hardening, and the proposed security boundary.
